userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: Ford Foundation has title, copyright and literary rights in the collection, in so far as it holds them.

The Rockefeller Archive Center has authority to grant permission to cite and publish material from the collection. Permission to publish extensive excerpts, or material in its entirety, will be referred to the Ford Foundation.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Ford Foundation archive was deposited at the RAC in 2011. Ford Foundation records, correspondence, reports, program files, and officers' papers were transferred to and accessioned by the RAC beginning in 2011. Accessions continue as necessary.
This material was transferred to the RAC as part of two larger accessions in 2021and 2024. These accessions were ingested by the RAC as Accessions 2021:067 and 2024:005.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The collection is comprised of five series. The fourth series is made up of two subseries.
Original order was maintained as much as possible.
The collection arrangement is as follows:
Subseries 4.1. Turkey Program – Beirut, Lebanon Field Office, 1951-1960
Subseries 4.2. Turkey Program – Ankara, Turkey Field Office, 1951-1972

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: The Ford Foundation's Field Office in Ankara, Turkey operated between 1960 and 1972. Situated within the Foundation's Middle East and Africa Program, it managed the Foundation's programming for Turkey. Support to Turkey through the Ankara Office and the broader Middle East and Africa Program, during these years, largely focused around developing math and science education, business and industrial development, family planning, library and library education development, and English language training.

The Ford Foundation's assistance to Turkey started in 1952 and was first administered through the Foundation's Near East Program Office in Beirut, Lebanon. In 1959, the Near East Program assigned a resident consultant representative to Turkey in addition to consultant representatives to Iran and the United Arab Republic. Eugene P. Northrop was assigned this post for Turkey. He later became Representative for Turkey when the Foundation established the Ankara Office in 1960.

The Ankara Office's program staff started to expand in 1965 with the addition of assistant representatives and program advisors. Northrop died in 1969. The Ankara Office did not have another full Representative between that time and its closing.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The collection contains the files of the Ford Foundation's Ankara, Turkey Field Office. In addition to files originating from within the Ankara Office, there are also earlier files created by the Foundation's Near East Program Office in Beirut, Lebanon which administered the Foundation's programming in Turkey before the Ankara Office opened. Together, these files provide broader insight into the Foundation's program activities in Turkey from the 1950s through the early 1970s when the Ankara Office closed in 1972.

The collection is made up of five series. The first three series contain files pertaining to Ford Foundation staff meetings, trips by Ankara Foundation Representative Eugene Northrop, and external conferences.

Comprising the bulk of the collection's contents, the fourth series contains subject files documenting the Foundation's Turkey program activities. This series has two subseries. The first subseries holds subject files created by the Beirut Field Office, and the second subseries holds subject files created by the Ankara Field Office.
The fifth series holds a small number of files concerning consultants supported by the Ankara Field Office and Ankara program staff acting as consultants for other Ford Foundation field offices.

Files document the Foundation working with and supporting Turkish government agencies, universities in Turkey, Turkey-based organizations, and international organizations. They show program interests in:

- Education development – Math and science education, teacher training, international schools, educational films and television, vocational education, international training and research, technical education, English language training
- Economic development – Industrial development, management training
- Family planning
- Library and library education development
- Agricultural development

The materials also document office operations outside of program activities and provide insight into Turkey and the Middle East at that time from the point of view of American Foundation staff working with and in the region.

Common material formats contained within the collection include correspondence, memos, reports, proposals, notes, travel itineraries, meeting materials, press clippings, newsletters, and several photographs.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Files in this series pertain to internal Ford Foundation staff meetings involving the Foundation's Ankara, Turkey Field Office. The meetings documented in the series include Foundation Representatives' meetings for the Foundation's Near East Program, Middle East and Africa Program, and Overseas Development Program/International Division. Topics of these meetings represent program priorities of the Foundation's Turkey programming such as agriculture, economic development, and education.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains trip files created by the Ford Foundation's Representative for Turkey Eugene Northrop. Northrop took these trips to other countries in the Middle East region, the United States, Latin America, and other areas.

The contents of the files demonstrate how Northrop's trips intersected with interests of the Foundation's Turkey programming such as the advancement of science education. The focus on science education advancement in the Latin American countries Northrop visited can be further explored in the "Science" subject files in Series 4

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains subject files documenting the Ford Foundation's program activities for Turkey between the 1950s and early 1970s. It is made up of two subseries. The first subseries contains files created by the Foundation's Near East Program Office in Beirut, Lebanon. The Beirut Office managed the Foundation's Turkey programming before the Foundation opened its office in Ankara, Turkey. Files created and maintained by the Ankara Office are contained in the second subseries.
Both subseries document the Ford Foundation's support for various areas in Turkey including education, management and industrial development, and family planning.

did.unittitle: Turkey Program - Beirut, Lebanon Field Office

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The subseries contains subject files documenting the Ford Foundation's program activities for Turkey that were created by the Foundation's Near East Program Office in Beirut, Lebanon. The files highlight the Near East Program Office's support for education in Turkey including assistance to universities, secondary education, and teacher training.
Kenneth Iverson served as the Near East Representative and contributed to the creation of the documents in the subseries.

did.unittitle: Education - American Girls' School, American College, American School for Boys
did.physdesc: The file contains 1 still image. The image is a photograph.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The photograph in the file includes a handwritten caption on the back. The photo is dated November 14, 1955, and it is described as showing a new building at the American Academy for Girls in Istanbul, Turkey. This building is likely Martin Hall. The Ford Foundation helped fund the American Academy for Girls to reconstruct its buildings with a grant in 1953. The American Academy for Girls is now the Uskudar American Academy (UAA).

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The subseries contains subject files documenting the Ford Foundation's program activities for Turkey that were created throughout the lifespan of the Foundation's Field Office in Ankara, Turkey. The files highlight the Turkey program's support for management and industrial development, science education development with assistance to institutions like the Middle East Technical University (METU) and Representative Eugene Northrop's trips throughout various Latin American countries and other regions on the subject, and family planning with assistance to Turkey based family planning organizations like the Hacettepe Institute of Population Studies and international organizations like the Population Council.
Several files are also devoted to the specific reports, memoranda, and correspondence produced by Representative Northrop.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains files concerning consultants supported by the Ford Foundation's Ankara, Turkey Field Office and consultancies performed by Ankara Field Office program staff for other Foundation field offices.

The consultants the Ankara Field Office supported to work in Turkey largely focused on science and science education. A few consultants were based at the Middle East Technical University (METU), and a few supported the National Science Lise Project.

Robert Kerwin who served as a Program Advisor for the Ford Foundation's Turkey programming (based in Istanbul) completed several consultancy trips to other Ford Foundation country offices. These consultancies were related to management development.
